newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines rejects call to slap reserves on FCDUs.
newsitem.headline: Philippines rejects call to slap reserves on FCDUs.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson rejected on Thursday a suggestion by the World Bank that it impose reserve requirements on foreign currency deposit units (FCDUs).

"I am not prepared to recommend to the Monetary Board the imposition of a reserve requirement on foreign currency deposits as some quarters have suggested, allegedly to equalise the burden between local and foreign currency deposits," Singson said in a speech to financial executives.
Singson added the move would be "unrealistic and counter-productive".
The World Bank had suggested that FCDUs have the same regulations as those imposed on peso deposits.
At present, peso deposits are subject to a 16 percent reserve requirement, as part the Central Bank's liquidity management.
"In a world of mobile capital and intensifying global financial market competition, this policy will be unrealistic and counter-productive," Singson said.
